g.text: Where is the Tathāgata to be found?
“An Arahant is annihilated at the breaking up of the body,
and does not exist after death.”
This takes for granted a ‘Tathāgata’ that can be found as a thing —
and then asks whether it is cut off or lasts. Sāriputta checks the first step.
Or is he in the aggregate(s)?
The Tathāgata cannot be grasped in any of these ways.
NOT APPREHENDED — EVEN IN THIS VERY LIFE
Yamaka: “my view is abandoned; I have made the breakthrough.”
Even the most revered image, once held as a thing, stands in the road.
CLUNG TO AS A THING · THE ROAD IS BLOCKED
the image, grasped — in or apart from the five
SEEN AS IT IS · THE ROAD IS OPEN
seen as it is: not the five, not in, not apart
The friendly attendant is the murderer all along — and the host never knows.
Alone, he takes the host’s life.
THE LEARNED DISCIPLE DOES NOT ENGAGE, CLING, OR RESOLVE: “THIS IS MY SELF”
No image of self, no image of the Buddha as a thing to hold —
“my mind is liberated from the taints through not clinging.”
